predecessors.name: Ptolemaic Kingdom
predecessors.text: Cyrene and Cyrenaica, 'awarded' to Ptolemy VIII by Roman intervention; Ptolemy VI kept Egypt and Cyprus

successors.name: Ptolemaic Kingdom
successors.text: Cyrene, rejoined to Egypt and Cyprus when the Alexandrians called on Ptolemy VIII to return from Cyrene in 145

ledger.x: 163 BCE: Rome gives Cyrene to Ptolemy VIII.
163 BCE: Cyrene and Cyrenaica pass from Ptolemy VI's kingdom to Ptolemy VIII.
162 BCE: 'He regained control over Cyrene by the end of 162 BC'; the page does not say whether by negotiation or force.
161 BCE: Ptolemy VIII invades Cyprus, which the Romans had promised him; Cypriot resistance forced him to abandon it after up to a year (the ptolemaic-kingdom dossier reads the page the same way).
160 BCE: the Cyprus expedition is abandoned (the page dates the expedition 161).
154 BCE: Ptolemy VI besieges his brother on Cyprus.
154 BCE: Ptolemy VIII withdraws from Cyprus.
145 BCE: Ptolemy VIII returns to Alexandria and Cyrene rejoins Egypt.
145 BCE: the separate kingdom of Cyrene ends.

wars.name: Ptolemy VIII's Cyprus expeditions
wars.outcome: The first (161) failed against Cypriot resistance; in 154 Ptolemy VI besieged him at Lapethus and he left Cyprus 'in exchange for continued possession of Cyrenaica'.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier for Ptolemy VIII's Cyrene.
